title: Yankees Crush Red Sox in Wild Card Game 2; Padres Surge Past Cubs – Live Scores 2026 MLB NBC Sports
body:
New York’s postseason drama reached a fever pitch on Tuesday as the Yankees dispatched the Boston Red Sox 6‑2 in the second Wild‑Card Game, while San Diego’s young club out‑pitched Chicago in a 4‑2 victory that gave the Padres a 2‑0 series lead. Both wins were decisive, ending the Red Sox’s brief resurgence and putting the Cubs on the brink of elimination as the two best‑of‑three Wild‑Card series moved into their final games.

The Yankees’ triumph was anchored by a dominant performance from right‑hander Gerrit Cole, who struck out nine batters over six innings while allowing just two runs. New York’s offense exploded early, with Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton each delivering a two‑run single in the third inning to turn a 1‑1 tie into a 5‑1 lead. Boston’s starter, Nathan Eovaldi, struggled to find his rhythm, surrendering three runs in the first two frames before being pulled in the fifth. Reliever Clarke Schmidt closed out the game, preserving the win and sending the Yankees to the Division Series with a 2‑1 series edge.

Across the country in San Diego, the Padres’ 4‑2 win over Chicago was a textbook example of strategic pitching and timely hitting. Starter Nick Pivetta, the former Red Sox left‑hander now with San Diego, delivered a solid 3 1/3‑inning outing, mixing fastballs and changeups to keep the Cubs off balance. He left with a 2‑1 lead, having allowed just one run on a solo home run by Javier Baez. The bullpen then took over, logging 5 2/3 consecutive scoreless frames. Veteran closer Josh Hader entered in the ninth and struck out two batters, sealing the victory and giving the Padres a 2‑0 advantage in the series.

The outcomes of both games underscore the shifting dynamics of the 2026 postseason. New York’s offensive firepower, which has been a hallmark all season, finally clicked after a tentative start to the series. The Yankees have now won three of the last four postseason games they have played, a trend that bodes well for their chances against the AL East champion Toronto Blue Jays, whom they will meet next week. Boston, on the other hand, appears to be in a familiar slump; the Red Sox have now lost five straight elimination games, a streak that has sparked calls for a reevaluation of their bullpen usage and lineup construction.

San Diego’s victory, meanwhile, highlights the rapid maturation of a roster that blended veteran savvy with youthful exuberance. The Padres’ front office has long touted their depth in pitching, and the performance of Pivetta—who was acquired in a mid‑season trade—demonstrates the payoff of that strategy. Chicago’s offense, which had been surging in the regular season, was stifled by a combination of precise pitch sequencing and aggressive defensive positioning. The Cubs now face a do‑or‑die Game 3, and their ability to rebound will likely hinge on whether their bullpen can replicate the dominance shown by the Padres’ relievers.

Looking ahead, the Yankees will travel to Toronto for a best‑of‑seven Division Series that promises a clash of contrasting styles: New York’s power‑hitting lineup versus Toronto’s small‑ball, speed‑driven approach. Meanwhile, the Padres will host the Atlanta Braves in the National League Division Series, where their pitching depth will be tested against a potent Atlanta offense led by Ronald Acuña Jr. and Austin Riley. Both teams have momentum on their side, but the short‑turn nature of postseason baseball means that a single misstep could end their campaigns.

If the Yankees can maintain their offensive rhythm and keep their bullpen fresh, they are positioned to advance to the AL Championship Series for the first time since 2022. The Padres, buoyed by a 2‑0 lead and a balanced staff, will aim to close out the Cubs and ride that confidence into Atlanta. As the Wild‑Card round concludes, the stage is set for compelling narratives to unfold in the next round, where every pitch and at‑bat will carry the weight of a city’s hopes.
